addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- codebase-memory: Use the codebase knowledge graph for structural code queries. Triggers on: explore the codebase, understand the architecture, what functions exist, show me the structure, who calls this function, what does X call, trace the call chain, find callers of, show dependencies, impact analysis, dead code, unused functions, high fan-out, refactor candidates, code quality audit, graph query syntax, Cypher query examples, edge types, how to use search_graph.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). content.text:
h06.

**Handlers (all in `server/router/api/v1/`, on `APIV1Service`):**

| RPC handler | Where the webhook path is entered |
|---|---|
| `CreateMemo` — `memo_service.go:70` | line 157 → `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` |
| `UpdateMemo` — `memo_service.go:401` | line 513 → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` → `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` (`memo_update_helpers.go:67`) |
| `DeleteMemo` — `memo_service.go:518` | line 562 → `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` |
| `CreateMemoComment` — `memo_service_comments.go:20` | line 119 → `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` |
| `SetMemoAttachments` — `memo_attachment_service.go:16` | line 48 → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` |
| `SetMemoRelations` — `memo_relation_service.go:16` | line 48 → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` |

**Convergence function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`**

All six handlers funnel into the dispatchers in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`, which load the target from `s.Store.GetUserWebhooks(...)` (the user-configured URL, stored per-user and set via `CreateUserWebhook`/`UpdateUserWebhook` in `user_service_webhooks.go`) and call `webhook.PostAsync` (lines 43 and 71). `PostAsync` only enqueues onto `asyncPostQueue`; the four worker goroutines started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`) are what call `Post`, which builds the `POST`, applies the optional HMAC-SHA256 Standard-Webhooks signature, and issues the request via `safeClient.Do` (line 152). There is no other caller of `Post` outside tests, so it is the sole delivery point.

Notes:
- `safeClient` uses `safeDialContext` (line 59), which resolves the host and rejects reserved/private IPs at dial time — SSRF/DNS-rebinding guard on top of the `webhook.ValidateURL` check done at configuration time.
- Other outbound-HTTP subsystems exist (`internal/httpgetter` for link metadata, `internal/ai`, `internal/idp`, `internal/storage`), but those are separate clients and do not pass through `webhook.Post`.
